short: A New York-class battleship that became the only remaining dreadnought in existence today, having fought in both World Wars.
full:
Commissioned on 12 March 1914, USS Texas (BB-35) was an American dreadnought battleship armed with ten 14-inch guns. Soon after entering service, she saw action in the Tampico Incident in Mexican waters. After the United States entered the First World War in 1917, she joined the Grand Fleet in the North Sea to bolster the Allied naval blockade against Germany.

Unlike most of her contemporaries, Texas survived the scrapping treaties of the interwar period and underwent extensive modernisation. In the Second World War, she provided vital naval gunfire support during the North African campaign, the Normandy landings, and the battles of Iwo Jima and Okinawa. She was decommissioned in 1948 to become a permanent museum ship, standing today as the last surviving dreadnought.
